text: It is significantly important to develop novel suppressor to achieve cobalt superconformal filling. Linear sweeping voltammetry (LSV) and impedance spectra (EIS) were coupled together to study the effect of novel dye suppressor nitrotetrazolium blue chloride (NBT) on cobalt electrodeposition. The adsorption behavior of NBT on cobalt substrate was investigated by applying density functional theory (DFT) calculation, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and in situ Raman spectra, while the interaction between NBT and cobalt ions ( Co ^ 2 +) is analyzed based on topology analysis and interaction region indicator (IRI) analysis. Synergistic suppressing mechanism, namely adsorption effect and coordination effect, was proposed to explain the suppressing effect of NBT during cobalt electrodeposition. The cobalt surface morphology analysis under the influence of NBT demonstrates that NBT is of grain refinement, while XRD analysis indicates that the formation of Co hcp (100) is formed preferentially. The superconformal filling of cobalt is achieved in microvias with different diameters. The cobalt layer is of excellent quality due to low surface deposit thickness (SDT). The SDT values are 15.9 μm, 8.8 μm and 4.9 μm for 150 m, 100 m and 50 m.

text: With semiconductor technology evolving continuously along the way based on Moore’s Law, the traditional copper damascene process is facing enormous challenges in terms of yield and reliability [1,2]. On one hand, when trench size is decreased to lower than Mean electron free path of copper, the intensified electron scattering at external surfaces and grain boundaries leads to the exponential growth of resistivity of copper interconnect, resulting in severely increased RC delay and IR drop [3,4]. On the other hand, the seed layer and barrier layer increase the proportion of non-conductive material within copper interconnect, further increasing the resistivity [5]. Meanwhile, it is hard to achieve void-defect filling of copper in downscaling interconnect line width since the current density at the opening is increased due to edge effect, which has a negative effect on reliability [6,7]. Among alternative metals, cobalt [8] is regarded as candidate interconnect metal as a result of low line resistivity at advanced node and compatibility to electroplating process compared with Ni [9,10], Ru [11], Au [12], graphene [13,14] etc.

text: Electroplating technology is key fabrication process to obtain cobalt interconnect [14]. It is essentially important to introduce proper additives to achieve superconformal growth of cobalt [15,16] since the growth rate at the plane and opening of vias is higher than that in the bottom and sidewalls as a result of mass transfer limitation within vias and edge effect at the opening [17,18]. Several additives used for cobalt superconformal filling has been reported in the literature. Josell et al. investigated branched polyethyleneimine (PEI) as suppressor and proposed S-shaped negative differential resistance (S-NDR) model to predict bottowm-up filling of cobalt [19], while Huang et al. studied the effect of oxime additive and believed that amine groups could coordinate with Co ^ 2 + to suppress the cobalt electrodeposition [20–22]. He et al. studied the influence of inhibitor polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) on cobalt electrodeposition as well as cobalt superconformal electrodeposition was achieved at trench with high aspect ratio [23]. In contrast, Ma et al. proposed adsorption-coordination inhibition mechanism to explain the suppressing effect of malachite green (MG) during cobalt electrodeposition and achieve superconformal filling [24].

text: Although several additives have been investigated, researchers pay little attention to the suppressing mechanism and effective special groups of additives based on experimental analysis and theoretical analysis. Advanced analyzing methods, including in situ Fourier Trans form Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) [25], in situ Surface Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS) [26,27] and Scanning Tunneling Microscopy [28], are widely used to study the adsorption behavior of additives. Besides, another emerging method, theoretical calculation is regarded as an effective method for exploiting the suppressing mechanism of additive [29]. For example, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation is widely accepted to analyze the adsorption ability of additive [30,31], while density functional theory (DFT) is often used to predict the effect of additive based on calculated parameters [32] and analyze interaction between metal ions and additive [33,34]. As a result, operando method and theoretical calculation can help researchers better understand the influencing mechanism, which can provide support for future molecule design.

text: In this work, a kind of dye molecule Nitrotetrazolium Blue chloride (NBT), was used as novel suppressor on cobalt electrodeposition. Electrochemical methods including linear sweeping voltammetry (LSV) and electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS) were used together to study the influence of NBT on kinetics of Co ^ 2 + reduction. Density functional theory (DFT) calculation was accepted to obtain the quantum chemical parameters of NBT. Besides, theoretical calculation, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and in situ Raman spectra were used to study the adsorption of NBT on cobalt substrate. Topology analysis and interaction region indicator (IRI) analysis were accepted to study the coordination between NBT and cobalt ions ( Co ^ 2 +). The suppressing mechanism of NBT is explained by proposing synergistic suppressing mechanism. The influence of NBT on morphology and crystal orientation is investi gated by SEM and XRD, respectively. Cobalt superconformal growth is achieved at microvias with different diameters.

text: Fig. 1 (a) shows the effect of NBT on electrochemical reaction. Generally, the increased cathodic polarization indicates that the metal electrodeposition is suppressed. In order to exclude the influence of NBT on hydrogen evolution reaction, LSV curves were measured without the existence of cobalt ions, as shown in Fig. S1. It can be seen that NBT can improve HER at a limited extent. As a result, the strengthened cathodic polarization will reflect the suppressing effect of NBT on cobalt deposition. The cathodic polarization is −1.180 V when NBT concentration is 0 mg/L. After the introduction of NBT, it can be found that even trace NBT can effectively increase the overpotential (more than 35 mV for 5 mg/L). Besides, the cathodic polarization sees an increase from −1.215 V to lower than −1.250 V with NBT increasing from 5 mg/L to 20 mg/L, which illustrates that suppressing effect for the electrodeposition of cobalt is intensified with the increase of NBT concentration and NBT is an effective suppressor for cobalt electrodeposition.

text: Electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS) are also used to confirm the suppressing effect of NBT on Co ^ 2 + reduction, as shown in Fig. 1 (b) and Figs. S1 to S3. Generally, the reaction energy barrier increases with impedance ring diameters [40]. As a result, the phenomenon of increasing impedance ring diameters with NBT illustrates that the suppressing effect is intensified by NBT regardless of applied measuring potential, consistent with the analysis from Fig. 1 (a). Besides, the equivalent circuit is established to calculate the charge transfer impedance (Rct) and solution impedance (Rs) by fitting parameters. The calculated results are shown in Fig. 1(c). Rs range from 30.1 to 30.8 Ω, indicating that NBT almost has no influence on solution impedance. The impedance with 5 mg/L is 596.6 Ω, far higher than that of VMS (400.5 Ω), which confirms that trace NBT can lead to strong cathodic polarization. When NBT is higher than 15 mg/L, the increased impedance become larger than 1250 Ω, which is two times higher than VMS, illustrating that NBT is of excellent suppressing effect during cobalt electrodeposition.

text: In summary, synergistic suppressing mechanism was proposed to illustrate the excellent suppressing ability of NBT during cobalt electrodeposition. On one hand, NBT is of excellent adsorption ability on cathodic surface since it is positively charged and is full of p i electron cloud of benzene and nitrogenous heterocyclic ring, which can reduce the active sites for reduction of Co ^ 2 + (Adsorption effect). On the other hand, the nitrogenous heterocyclic ring opening due to accepting electrons from cathodic surface leads to that NBT can coordinate with Co ^ 2 + when Co ^ 2 + go through the NBT adsorption layer, which further increase the energy barrier (Coordination effect).

text: The effect of NBT on cobalt layer morphology was studied by SEM, as shown in Fig. 6. The inserted figure shows the grain size distribution and mean grain size. The cobalt layer is relatively compact when NBT ranges from 0 mg/L to 15 mg/L. However, it should be noted that the cobalt layer is full of large and coarse grains (mean grain size of about 416 nm) without NBT. The quality of cobalt layer can be effectively improved by introducing NBT, as shown in Fig. 6 (b) to (d). The cobalt layer becomes more uniform when NBT concentration rises from 5 mg/L to 15 mg/L, indicating that NBT can improve the surface morphology. Besides, the grain size is about 356 nm when NBT concentration is 5 mg/L. In contrast, the grain size is reduced to about 264 nm and lower than 240 nm when NBT concentration is 10 mg/L and 15 mg/L, respectively. The phenomenon of decreased grain size with rising of NBT concentration indicates that NBT is of grain refinement and the improved surface smoothness is conducive to lowering the losses of signal transmission.

text: The superconformal growth of cobalt within microvias is achieved to confirm the effect of NBT, as shown in Fig. 8. The current transients are provided in supplementary (Fig. S5) and the current density is about 1.6 mA/cm2 while calculated current efficiency is 40 %. Fig. 8 (a) shows the shape evolution in microvias of 150 μm during cobalt electrodeposition. The cobalt electrodeposition at the opening of microvias is effectively suppressed due to fast mass transfer of NBT near the plane and opening. In contrast, the supplementary rate of NBT at the bottom is lowered than consuming rate as a result of relatively slow mass transfer of NBT from bulk solution into microvias. Cobalt layer began to grow from the bottom to the top of the microvias, as shown in a2 (8h) in Fig. 8 (a). After being electrodeposited for 16 h, cobalt layer grows near the opening of microvias while the surface deposit thickness (SDT) is lowered than 16 μm, indicating that NBT is of excellent selectivity.
